what_this_is: The Workshop row for the tool in tools/read-a-list-view: one page of what a person's list or saved view shows, its own rows and its row sources' rows, read through the person's own door.

payload.label: Read a page of one of my lists or saved views
payload.job: Read one page of what one of my lists shows, its own rows and then the rows of each row source it declares (a folder of documents, for one), or what a saved view of it keeps, in its order
payload.description: Reads the list (or the saved view and its list) through the person's door. Its own rows come first, then each row source's rows, each source read by running the tool that serves it (read-data/list-view.json), so nothing is copied. A page holds `limit` rows (the lists' read_page_rows when left out, never more than rows_per_read) and answers `next` while more remain. A view with rules keeps the rows the person's rule-filter tool says its rules keep, ordered by its sort. A list with more row sources than its bound, a source no tool serves, or a source that answers no rows is refused, never shown as empty.

config.description: The person's door config file (the README describes its keys).

list.description: The list's id; give this or view.

view.description: The saved view's record id; give this or list.

after.description: The `next` of the page before; left out for the first page.

output_schema.description: { list, fields, rows: [{ id, values, title, source? }], next, complete } as JSON; exit 2 with the reason on standard error.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout, and reads their lists through their own door with their own key. Use --view instead of --list for a saved view. Show the rows as a table of the list's fields, and read the next page with `next` until it is null when they want every row.

provenance.source: Written for the Workshop: a list read that pages across a list's own records and its row sources, in the way a database view joins its tables
